SC1_cache_leak.verdict: FIXED and measured on both builds
SC1_cache_leak.mechanism_chosen: no-store on the three public watch-document reads in lib/video.server.ts
SC1_cache_leak.why_not_a_shorter_window: Next's data cache does not replace a cached successful body with a FAILED revalidation, so the entry never clears — the window length is irrelevant; ANY window leaks indefinitely once the video 404s.
SC1_cache_leak.why_not_tag_invalidation: tag-based revalidation would need vidra-core to call back into the frontend; there is no such channel
SC1_cache_leak.cost_per_page_view: one uncached GET /api/v1/videos/{id} per watch-page RENDER (not two: React cache() still deduplicates generateMetadata and the page body within one pass). Previously concurrent views of one video could share a single backend read for up to 60 s. The home page's featured-banner read is also uncached now, but /app/page.tsx was already dynamic because lib/feed.server.ts is no-store, so that page gains one request and loses no caching tier.

SC2_rejection_note.verdict: FIXED — stored, delivered to the creator, read back by staff
SC2_rejection_note.stored_where: video_rejections (0130), one row, note + rejected_by + created_at
SC2_rejection_note.creator_surface: GET /me/notifications -> the video_rejected item's moderation_note; rendered in the inbox as 'A moderator rejected your upload “Held Upload” — it was not published: <note>' after a hard navigation
SC2_rejection_note.staff_surface: GET /admin/videos -> moderation_note on the inventory row; rendered at /moderation/videos as 'Rejected: <note>' under the state pills. A rejected video has left the quarantine queue, so this is the only staff surface it still appears on.
SC2_rejection_note.audit_row: unchanged: Reason='moderator_rejected' plus metadata reason_provided=true|false. A SQL sweep of audit_log for the note's text returned 0 rows.
SC2_rejection_note.deviation_from_the_brief: SC2 asked for the note in 'the audit row's structured payload'. That is not implementable and would have been a regression: audit.normalizeEvent validates metadata against a CLOSED key allowlist with a 256-byte value cap and states 'user prose, URLs, payloads, headers and process output never belong here'; an unknown key or an over-long value makes the WHOLE event invalid (ErrInvalidEvent), so a 2000-character note would have deleted the audit row rather than enriched it. TestQuarantineRejectNotifiesOwner also already asserted the prose does not reach the log stream, and weakening a test was not an option. The note therefore lives in the moderation domain and the ledger keeps the classification.
SC2_rejection_note.moderator_identity: still never exposed — the notification's actor is null

SC3_creator_visible_block.verdict: FIXED for the owner's listing and the notification; the single-video Studio deep link is recorded, not changed
SC3_creator_visible_block.owner_listing: GET /channels/{handle}/videos read by someone who can manage the channel now carries blocked:true (SQL EXISTS on video_blocks). Measured: state stays 'published' and privacy stays 'public' — a block changes neither, which is why the marker had to be its own column.
SC3_creator_visible_block.notification_type: video_blocked — a NEW type. video_rejected did not fit: it means an upload that NEVER published, while a block takes down live content and is reversible, and reusing it would have told the creator their upload was never published. KnownTypes(), knownType(), the preference default and the frontend renderer + prefs label all learned it, TDD.
SC3_creator_visible_block.reason_visibility: NOT shown to the creator. The notification payload was checked for the block reason string across the whole response: absent. The Studio row says 'Blocked by moderation — this video is not available to viewers, including you, until a moderator lifts the block. Nothing else about it has changed.'

SC3_creator_visible_block.unfixed_and_recorded: /studio?video={id} (ManagedVideoView) still shows its generic error for the owner of a blocked video, because it fetches GET /videos/{id}, which 404s for them. Opening that read would flip a measured promise (watch detail 404 for the owner) and was deliberately not done; the creator reaches the same video, badged, from /studio/content.

findings_recorded_not_fixed: The Studio single-video deep link /studio?video={id} still errors for the owner of a BLOCKED video, because GET /videos/{id} 404s for them.
Unblocking sends the creator no notification, so a creator learns their video is back only by looking.
The watch route answers 200 with a loading shell for a blocked, deleted or unknown video rather than 404 (pre-existing; no content leaks).
A creator can still PATCH a blocked video's metadata (the update path has no block gate) while they cannot read it — inconsistent, inert, and out of scope here.
Reason-visibility for BLOCKS is an open product ruling: the block reason is currently staff-only. Rejection notes are shown, blocks are not, and that asymmetry is deliberate but unratified.
for_a16_slice_3_and_the_admin_follow_up: The fake-fidelity lesson bit again: videoFakeRepo's ListVideosByChannel had to learn video_blocks before the owner-marker test could prove anything. Mute/watched-word predicates will have the same shape — mirror the SQL in the fake FIRST.

A new notification type costs four edits that must move together: the constant, knownType(), KnownTypes(), and the frontend TYPE_LABELS + TYPE_ORDER + describeNotification case. A missing describeNotification case falls through to 'started following'.
audit_log cannot carry prose. Any slice that wants a moderator's words persisted needs a moderation-domain table; the ledger takes a classification only.
An inline ': ' inside a plain-scalar OpenAPI description parses in Go and BREAKS the frontend codegen's YAML loader. Use an em dash or a block scalar.
PATCH /admin/instance-settings takes a FLAT object ({"quarantine_new_uploads":true}); {"settings":{...}} is 422.
A synthetic mp4 fails the ffprobe media probe and the upload lands `failed` — generate a real clip with ffmpeg.
